exampleFr: Mon chien adore jouer dans le jardin.
exampleEn: My dog loves playing in the garden.

exampleFr: Le chat dort toute la journée sur le canapé.
exampleEn: The cat sleeps all day on the sofa.
collocations: avoir un chat dans la gorge
mnemonic: The English idiom 'a frog in your throat' becomes 'un chat dans la gorge' (a cat in the throat) in French.

exampleFr: Le chaton joue avec une pelote de laine.
exampleEn: The kitten plays with a ball of wool.

exampleFr: Le chiot mordille tous les meubles de la maison.
exampleEn: The puppy nibbles on all the furniture in the house.

exampleFr: Le lapin mange une carotte dans son enclos.
exampleEn: The rabbit is eating a carrot in its pen.
mnemonic: 'Poser un lapin' (literally 'to put down a rabbit') means to stand someone up.

exampleFr: Mon petit frère a un hamster dans une cage.
exampleEn: My little brother has a hamster in a cage.
mnemonic: 'Hamster' starts with an aspirated h in French, so no elision: 'le hamster', not 'l'hamster'.

exampleFr: Une souris grise a traversé la cuisine hier soir.
exampleEn: A grey mouse ran across the kitchen last night.
mnemonic: 'Souris' is invariable in the plural: 'une souris' → 'des souris' — also the word for a computer mouse!

exampleFr: Les vaches broutent tranquillement dans le pré.
exampleEn: The cows are grazing peacefully in the meadow.

exampleFr: Le cochon se roule dans la boue pour se rafraîchir.
exampleEn: The pig rolls in the mud to cool off.

exampleFr: Le berger compte ses moutons avant la nuit.
exampleEn: The shepherd counts his sheep before nightfall.

exampleFr: La poule pond un œuf presque tous les jours.
exampleEn: The hen lays an egg almost every day.
mnemonic: 'Avoir la chair de poule' (to have hen flesh) is how French says 'to have goosebumps'.

exampleFr: Le coq chante très fort dès le lever du soleil.
exampleEn: The rooster crows very loudly at sunrise.
mnemonic: The rooster ('le coq gaulois') is an unofficial national symbol of France.

exampleFr: Les enfants donnent du pain aux canards du parc.
exampleEn: The children give bread to the ducks in the park.
mnemonic: 'Canard' is also French slang for a newspaper.

exampleFr: L'oie siffle fort quand un étranger approche.
exampleEn: The goose hisses loudly when a stranger approaches.

exampleFr: Elle monte à cheval tous les samedis matin.
exampleEn: She goes horseback riding every Saturday morning.
mnemonic: Irregular plural: 'un cheval' → 'des chevaux', like most nouns ending in -al.

exampleFr: L'âne porte de lourds sacs sur son dos.
exampleEn: The donkey carries heavy bags on its back.

exampleFr: La chèvre grimpe facilement sur les rochers.
exampleEn: The goat easily climbs onto the rocks.

exampleFr: Mes grands-parents habitent dans une ferme à la campagne.
exampleEn: My grandparents live on a farm in the countryside.

exampleFr: On mange traditionnellement de la dinde à Noël.
exampleEn: Turkey is traditionally eaten at Christmas.
mnemonic: 'Dinde' also means 'silly woman' in familiar speech, similar to English 'turkey' as an insult.

exampleFr: L'agneau naît souvent au printemps dans les fermes.
exampleEn: Lambs are often born in spring on farms.

exampleFr: Le poussin vient de sortir de son œuf.
exampleEn: The chick has just hatched from its egg.

exampleFr: L'écureuil grimpe rapidement au sommet du chêne.
exampleEn: The squirrel quickly climbs to the top of the oak tree.
mnemonic: Notoriously hard to pronounce: three vowel sounds packed into 'é-cu-reuil'.

exampleFr: Le renard rôde autour du poulailler la nuit.
exampleEn: The fox prowls around the henhouse at night.

exampleFr: On entend parfois le loup hurler dans la forêt.
exampleEn: You can sometimes hear the wolf howling in the forest.
mnemonic: 'Avoir une faim de loup' means to be extremely hungry (literally 'to have a wolf's hunger').

exampleFr: L'ours brun hiberne pendant tout l'hiver.
exampleEn: The brown bear hibernates all winter long.

exampleFr: Le lion est surnommé le roi des animaux.
exampleEn: The lion is nicknamed the king of the animals.

exampleFr: Le tigre chasse seul, contrairement au lion.
exampleEn: The tiger hunts alone, unlike the lion.

exampleFr: L'éléphant utilise sa trompe pour boire de l'eau.
exampleEn: The elephant uses its trunk to drink water.

exampleFr: Le singe saute d'une branche à l'autre.
exampleEn: The monkey jumps from one branch to another.

exampleFr: La girafe a un très long cou pour atteindre les feuilles.
exampleEn: The giraffe has a very long neck to reach the leaves.

exampleFr: Le panda géant se nourrit presque uniquement de bambou.
exampleEn: The giant panda feeds almost exclusively on bamboo.

exampleFr: Le cerf traverse la clairière au lever du jour.
exampleEn: The stag crosses the clearing at dawn.
mnemonic: Final 'f' is silent: 'cerf' rhymes with 'air'. Fun fact: 'un cerf-volant' (literally 'a flying stag') means 'a kite'.

exampleFr: Le hérisson se roule en boule dès qu'il se sent menacé.
exampleEn: The hedgehog rolls into a ball as soon as it feels threatened.
mnemonic: 'Hérisson' has an aspirated h: no elision, no liaison — 'le hérisson', 'les hérissons' (no linking sound).

exampleFr: Un sanglier a traversé la route devant notre voiture.
exampleEn: A wild boar crossed the road in front of our car.

exampleFr: Le blaireau creuse un terrier profond dans la forêt.
exampleEn: The badger digs a deep burrow in the forest.
mnemonic: 'Blaireau' can also be a mild insult meaning 'idiot' in familiar French, and also means 'shaving brush'.

exampleFr: La taupe creuse des galeries sous la pelouse.
exampleEn: The mole digs tunnels under the lawn.
mnemonic: Just like in English, 'une taupe' can also mean a spy or informant hidden inside an organization.

exampleFr: La chauve-souris se déplace grâce à l'écholocation.
exampleEn: The bat navigates using echolocation.
mnemonic: Literally 'bald mouse' — 'chauve' (bald) + 'souris' (mouse), describing its hairless wings.

exampleFr: Un oiseau chante sur la branche devant ma fenêtre.
exampleEn: A bird is singing on the branch outside my window.

exampleFr: Des pigeons se rassemblent sur la place tous les matins.
exampleEn: Pigeons gather in the square every morning.
mnemonic: 'Pigeon' also means 'a sucker, an easy target' in informal French.

exampleFr: L'oiseau construit son nid avec des brindilles.
exampleEn: The bird builds its nest with twigs.

exampleFr: Le papillon bat des ailes lentement au soleil.
exampleEn: The butterfly slowly flaps its wings in the sun.

exampleFr: L'arrivée des hirondelles annonce le printemps.
exampleEn: The arrival of the swallows announces spring.
collocations: une hirondelle ne fait pas le printemps
mnemonic: French saying: 'une hirondelle ne fait pas le printemps' — one swallow doesn't make spring (don't draw conclusions too fast).

exampleFr: Des moineaux picorent des miettes de pain sur le trottoir.
exampleEn: Sparrows are pecking at bread crumbs on the sidewalk.

exampleFr: Un corbeau noir croasse depuis la cime du sapin.
exampleEn: A black crow is cawing from the top of the fir tree.
mnemonic: 'Un corbeau' can also mean 'an anonymous letter writer' in French, from the 1943 film Le Corbeau.

exampleFr: Le hibou chasse ses proies pendant la nuit.
exampleEn: The owl hunts its prey at night.
mnemonic: One of the rare words that adds -x instead of -s in the plural: 'un hibou' → 'des hiboux'. Also aspirated h: 'le hibou'.

exampleFr: Le cygne blanc glisse gracieusement sur le lac.
exampleEn: The white swan glides gracefully across the lake.
mnemonic: Don't confuse with 'signe' (sign) — same pronunciation, completely different word.

exampleFr: L'aigle plane au-dessus de la vallée à la recherche d'une proie.
exampleEn: The eagle soars above the valley looking for prey.

exampleFr: La pie est réputée pour voler les objets brillants.
exampleEn: The magpie is known for stealing shiny objects.
mnemonic: 'Bavard comme une pie' (chatty as a magpie) describes someone who never stops talking.

exampleFr: Le chant mélancolique du rossignol résonnait dans la nuit.
exampleEn: The nightingale's melancholic song echoed through the night.
mnemonic: A favourite bird of French poets for its beautiful nighttime song, frequently evoked in classical poetry.

exampleFr: L'abeille butine les fleurs du jardin toute la journée.
exampleEn: The bee gathers pollen from the garden flowers all day.

exampleFr: Il s'est fait piquer par une guêpe pendant le pique-nique.
exampleEn: He got stung by a wasp during the picnic.

exampleFr: Un papillon coloré se pose sur la fleur.
exampleEn: A colourful butterfly lands on the flower.
mnemonic: 'Nager le papillon' is the swimming stroke 'the butterfly'.

exampleFr: Les fourmis transportent des miettes vers leur fourmilière.
exampleEn: The ants carry crumbs back to their anthill.
collocations: avoir des fourmis dans les jambes
mnemonic: 'Avoir des fourmis dans les jambes' means to have pins and needles (literally 'ants in the legs').

exampleFr: Une grosse araignée a tissé sa toile dans le coin du garage.
exampleEn: A big spider spun its web in the corner of the garage.
mnemonic: 'Avoir une araignée au plafond' (to have a spider on the ceiling) means to be a bit crazy.

exampleFr: Les moustiques nous ont piqués toute la soirée.
exampleEn: The mosquitoes bit us all evening.

exampleFr: Une mouche tourne autour de la table depuis ce matin.
exampleEn: A fly has been circling the table since this morning.
mnemonic: 'Prendre la mouche' means to get offended easily over nothing.

exampleFr: L'escargot avance très lentement sur la pierre mouillée.
exampleEn: The snail moves very slowly on the wet stone.

exampleFr: Une coccinelle rouge s'est posée sur mon doigt.
exampleEn: A red ladybug landed on my finger.

exampleFr: Des libellules survolent la surface de l'étang.
exampleEn: Dragonflies fly over the surface of the pond.

exampleFr: Nous avons pêché trois poissons ce matin.
exampleEn: We caught three fish this morning.
collocations: être heureux comme un poisson dans l'eau
mnemonic: 'Être heureux comme un poisson dans l'eau' means to be completely at ease (happy as a fish in water).

exampleFr: Les dauphins nagent en groupe près du bateau.
exampleEn: The dolphins swim in a group near the boat.

exampleFr: La baleine bleue est le plus grand animal du monde.
exampleEn: The blue whale is the largest animal in the world.

exampleFr: Un requin a été aperçu près de la côte hier.
exampleEn: A shark was spotted near the coast yesterday.

exampleFr: La tortue avance lentement mais sûrement vers la mer.
exampleEn: The turtle moves slowly but surely towards the sea.

exampleFr: Le crabe se cache rapidement sous une pierre.
exampleEn: The crab quickly hides under a rock.

exampleFr: Le phoque se prélasse sur les rochers au soleil.
exampleEn: The seal is basking on the rocks in the sun.

exampleFr: Attention, il y a des méduses près de la plage aujourd'hui.
exampleEn: Watch out, there are jellyfish near the beach today.
mnemonic: Named after Medusa from Greek mythology, because of its tentacle-like stinging arms.

exampleFr: Le restaurant sert du homard grillé le week-end.
exampleEn: The restaurant serves grilled lobster on weekends.
mnemonic: Aspirated h: 'le homard', never 'l'homard'.

exampleFr: On mange traditionnellement des huîtres à Noël en France.
exampleEn: Oysters are traditionally eaten at Christmas in France.
mnemonic: Mute h here, unlike 'homard': 'l'huître', 'les huîtres' (with liaison).

exampleFr: Le serpent se glisse silencieusement entre les rochers.
exampleEn: The snake slithers silently between the rocks.

exampleFr: Le lézard se réchauffe au soleil sur le mur.
exampleEn: The lizard is warming itself in the sun on the wall.
mnemonic: 'Faire le lézard' (informal) means to laze around in the sun.

exampleFr: La grenouille saute d'un nénuphar à l'autre.
exampleEn: The frog jumps from one lily pad to another.

exampleFr: Un gros crapaud attend patiemment près de la mare.
exampleEn: A big toad waits patiently near the pond.

exampleFr: Le crocodile reste immobile juste sous la surface de l'eau.
exampleEn: The crocodile stays motionless just below the water's surface.
mnemonic: 'Des larmes de crocodile' (crocodile tears) means fake, insincere tears — same idiom as in English.

exampleFr: Nous nous sommes promenés dans la forêt tout l'après-midi.
exampleEn: We walked through the forest all afternoon.

exampleFr: Elle plante des tomates dans son jardin chaque été.
exampleEn: She plants tomatoes in her garden every summer.

exampleFr: Nous passons nos vacances d'hiver à la montagne.
exampleEn: We spend our winter holidays in the mountains.

exampleFr: La mer est calme ce matin, parfaite pour nager.
exampleEn: The sea is calm this morning, perfect for swimming.
mnemonic: 'La mer' (sea) and 'la mère' (mother) are homophones — spelling is the only difference.

exampleFr: Ils font du canoë sur le lac tous les dimanches.
exampleEn: They go canoeing on the lake every Sunday.

exampleFr: Les enfants pêchent des truites dans la rivière.
exampleEn: The children fish for trout in the river.

exampleFr: On passe l'après-midi à la plage à construire des châteaux de sable.
exampleEn: We spend the afternoon at the beach building sandcastles.

exampleFr: Le fermier laboure le champ avant les semailles.
exampleEn: The farmer plows the field before sowing.
mnemonic: Same root as 'les Champs-Élysées' — literally 'the Elysian Fields'.

exampleFr: Nous avons ramassé des champignons dans le bois.
exampleEn: We picked mushrooms in the woods.
mnemonic: 'Bois' also means 'wood' as a material — and is the imperative 'drink!' from 'boire'. Context makes it clear.

exampleFr: Il fait extrêmement chaud le jour dans le désert.
exampleEn: It is extremely hot during the day in the desert.

exampleFr: Nous avons pris un bateau pour rejoindre l'île.
exampleEn: We took a boat to reach the island.

exampleFr: Ils ont acheté une maison à la campagne pour se reposer.
exampleEn: They bought a house in the countryside to relax.

exampleFr: Le village est construit au sommet d'une colline.
exampleEn: The village is built on top of a hill.

exampleFr: La rivière serpente à travers toute la vallée.
exampleEn: The river winds through the whole valley.

exampleFr: La Loire est le plus long fleuve de France.
exampleEn: The Loire is the longest river in France.
mnemonic: French distinguishes 'un fleuve' (flows into the sea) from 'une rivière' (flows into another river) — English just says 'river' for both.

exampleFr: Les falaises d'Étretat attirent des milliers de touristes.
exampleEn: The cliffs of Étretat attract thousands of tourists.

exampleFr: Les randonneurs ont atteint le sommet avant midi.
exampleEn: The hikers reached the summit before noon.

exampleFr: Cet arbre perd toutes ses feuilles en automne.
exampleEn: This tree loses all its leaves in autumn.

exampleFr: Elle offre un bouquet de fleurs pour son anniversaire.
exampleEn: She gives a bouquet of flowers for his birthday.

exampleFr: Les enfants jouent pieds nus dans l'herbe fraîche.
exampleEn: The children play barefoot in the fresh grass.
mnemonic: Mute h: 'l'herbe', 'les herbes' (with liaison).

exampleFr: Les feuilles deviennent rouges et oranges en automne.
exampleEn: The leaves turn red and orange in autumn.
mnemonic: 'Feuille' also means 'sheet of paper' — une feuille de papier.

exampleFr: L'oiseau est perché sur une branche basse.
exampleEn: The bird is perched on a low branch.

exampleFr: Les racines de cet arbre s'étendent très loin sous terre.
exampleEn: This tree's roots extend very far underground.

exampleFr: Elle arrose ses plantes tous les deux jours.
exampleEn: She waters her plants every two days.

exampleFr: Il a offert une rose rouge à sa femme.
exampleEn: He gave a red rose to his wife.
mnemonic: 'Rose' is also the colour pink and a common first name — the flower gave its name to the colour.

exampleFr: Une épaisse couche de mousse recouvre les pierres humides.
exampleEn: A thick layer of moss covers the damp stones.
mnemonic: 'Mousse' also means foam, and even chocolate mousse — same word, very different things.

exampleFr: Des fougères poussent à l'ombre des grands arbres.
exampleEn: Ferns grow in the shade of the tall trees.

exampleFr: L'aigle vole très haut au-dessus des montagnes.
exampleEn: The eagle flies very high above the mountains.
mnemonic: 'Voler' also means 'to steal' — 'On m'a volé mon vélo' (My bike got stolen). Context tells the two meanings apart.

exampleFr: Les canards nagent tranquillement sur l'étang.
exampleEn: The ducks swim peacefully on the pond.

exampleFr: Chaque automne, ils plantent des bulbes de tulipes.
exampleEn: Every autumn, they plant tulip bulbs.

exampleFr: On a aperçu un cerf sauvage à l'orée du bois.
exampleEn: We spotted a wild deer at the edge of the woods.

exampleFr: Cette araignée n'est pas venimeuse pour l'homme.
exampleEn: This spider is not venomous to humans.
mnemonic: Don't confuse with 'vénéneux': 'venimeux' describes animals that inject venom by biting or stinging, while 'vénéneux' describes poisonous plants or mushrooms.

exampleFr: Le cheval hennit dès qu'il entend son propriétaire arriver.
exampleEn: The horse neighs as soon as it hears its owner arriving.

exampleFr: On entendait les vaches meugler depuis la route.
exampleEn: You could hear the cows mooing from the road.

exampleFr: Les moutons bêlaient bruyamment en attendant leur repas.
exampleEn: The sheep bleated loudly while waiting for their food.

exampleFr: La vache est un ruminant qui digère l'herbe en plusieurs étapes.
exampleEn: The cow is a ruminant that digests grass in several stages.
